ne4cbdfc64e4.s: Who became the first woman Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly in 1999?
ne4cbdfc64e4.x: Pratibha Bharati became the first woman Speaker of the AP Legislative Assembly in 1999. Sharda Mukherjee was the first woman Governor (1977).

n57e5d0aad5d.s: The Andhra Mahila Sabha was founded by:
n57e5d0aad5d.x: The Andhra Mahila Sabha was founded by Durgabai Deshmukh.

n16c767adba2.s: The Progressive Organisation of Women (POW) was founded in:
n16c767adba2.x: POW was founded in 1974; the Stree Shakti Sanghatana followed in 1978.

n3dbacab9bfe.s: The AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act was enacted in:
n3dbacab9bfe.x: The AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act is of 1988; the earlier Madras Act is of 1947.

nd673ca35378.s: Which Article reserves at least one-third of seats for women in Panchayats?
nd673ca35378.x: Article 243D(3), added by the 73rd Amendment (1992), covers Panchayats; Article 243T covers Municipalities.

n1f4fa3cee88.s: The journals Janana and Satihita Bodhini, which promoted women's education and widow remarriage, were associated with:
n1f4fa3cee88.x: Janana and Satihita Bodhini were Kandukuri Veeresalingam's journals promoting women's education and widow remarriage.

n97f7fdca3b6.s: The Second World Telugu Conference was held at:
n97f7fdca3b6.x: The Second World Telugu Conference was held at Kuala Lumpur; the First was at Hyderabad, the Third in Mauritius and the Fourth at Tirupati.

n884907801ac.s: Ravindra Bharathi, Hyderabad (1961), was built to mark the birth centenary of:
n884907801ac.x: Ravindra Bharathi was built in 1961 for Tagore's birth centenary, not Gandhi's.

n5e1ce9a4d76.s: The Sangeet Natak Akademi, the first national arts academy, was inaugurated by:
n5e1ce9a4d76.x: The Sangeet Natak Akademi, the first national arts academy, was inaugurated by Rajendra Prasad.

nfed258e8a7e.s: Gurram Jashuva received the Padma Bhushan in:
nfed258e8a7e.x: Jashuva received the Padma Bhushan in 1970; his Sahitya Akademi Award came in 1964.

nefde1da3701.s: Along with an annual Telugu Mahotsavam, Andhra Pradesh has proposed to revive the:
nefde1da3701.x: Andhra Pradesh announced an annual Telugu Mahotsavam to revive folk and theatre forms, and the Nandi Natakotsavams are also proposed to be revived.

n9575e7947bc.s: Which of the following Telugu film directors received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award?
n9575e7947bc.x: K. Viswanath is among the Telugu recipients of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, along with B.N. Reddy and Akkineni Nageswara Rao.

ncc582430f09.s: The first communist Telugu journal was:
ncc582430f09.x: Prajasakti was the first communist Telugu journal; Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal after Independence.

nc36959f7fd9.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
nc36959f7fd9.x: Ramayana Vishavruksham is by Ranganayakamma. Veyi Padagalu is Viswanatha Satyanarayana's, Athadu Adavini Jayinchadu is Kesava Reddy's and Tulasidalam is Yandamuri Veerendranath's.

nf560293f3ac.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry only one date)
nf560293f3ac.s: Who was the first president of the Viplava Rachayitala Sangham (Virasam), founded in 1970?
nf560293f3ac.x: Virasam, founded on 4 July 1970, had Sri Sri as its first president, not Gaddar.

nc603195d961.s: C. Narayana Reddy received the Jnanpith Award in:
nc603195d961.x: C. Narayana Reddy received the Jnanpith in 1988; Viswanatha Satyanarayana in 1970 and Ravuri Bharadwaja in 2012.

n4db83d0b403.s: The Digambara kavulu, the anti-establishment movement of 'naked poets', began in:
n4db83d0b403.x: The Digambara movement began in 1965; 1970 is when several Digambaras moved to Virasam.

n8ee26b9c1d4.x: Baddam Bhaskara Reddy wrote as Cherabandaraju; Mahaswapna was the pen name of Kammisetti Venkateswara Rao.

nf7ae7085702.s: Which of the following pairs of film studio and founder is correctly matched?
o: Ramoji Film City – Akkineni Nageswara Rao
nf7ae7085702.x: Annapurna Studios, Hyderabad, was founded by Akkineni Nageswara Rao. Ramoji Film City was founded by Ramoji Rao and Vijaya Vauhini by B. Nagi Reddy and Aluri Chakrapani.

n94320e7387d.s: The first Telugu talkie, Bhakta Prahlada, was directed by:
n94320e7387d.x: Bhakta Prahlada was directed by H.M. Reddy, not C. Pullaiah.

nc3987b01585.s: In 2011, Chiranjeevi's Praja Rajyam Party merged with the:
nc3987b01585.x: The Praja Rajyam Party (founded 2008) merged with the Congress in 2011, not the TDP.

n6689f3d1817.s: Who is hailed as the 'godfather of the Telugu talkie'?
n6689f3d1817.x: H.M. Reddy, who assisted Ardeshir Irani on Alam Ara, is hailed as the godfather of the Telugu talkie.

nadc004e9190.s: Who received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2023 at the 71st National Film Awards?
nadc004e9190.x: Mohanlal received the Phalke Award for 2023 at the 71st National Film Awards; Anant Nag was named for 2024.

n75f64036f91.s: N.T. Rama Rao, who founded the TDP in March 1982, became Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in:
n75f64036f91.x: NTR became Chief Minister in 1983, within a year of founding the TDP on 29 March 1982.

n72519b421d9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Nagarjunakonda?
o: It has an acoustic building and an amphitheatre.
It has fewer than ten stupas.
It has Santamula's Ashvamedha altar and a Sati sculpture.
It shows habitation from the Palaeolithic to 1960 CE.
n72519b421d9.x: Nagarjunakonda has more than 30 stupas, so 'fewer than ten' is false; the other three features are all associated with the site.

n5a274bb59f5.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Victoria Jubilee Museum – Salar Jung Museum
n5a274bb59f5.x: The Baudhasree Archaeological Museum is at Guntur. Veiled Rebecca is in the Salar Jung Museum, and the Bapu Museum at Vijayawada was formerly the Victoria Jubilee Museum.

nc5e94cb9e39.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates for the sites)
nc5e94cb9e39.s: The Buddhist site of Salihundam was discovered by:
nc5e94cb9e39.x: Salihundam was discovered by Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy; A. Ranganatha Saraswati found Nagarjunakonda in 1926.

n86e9c374661.s: In Ugadi 2012, Bapu received the State's ____ award for painting.
n86e9c374661.x: Bapu, known for line drawings of epic characters, received the State's Telugu Velugu award for painting in Ugadi 2012.

n263a6bb4b9c.s: Lepakshi was placed on UNESCO's tentative list of World Heritage Sites in:
n263a6bb4b9c.x: Lepakshi, including the Veerabhadra temple and monolithic Nandi, was placed on the tentative list in 2022; Andhra Pradesh has no inscribed World Heritage Site.

n4979de6009f.s: The Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act was enacted in:
n4979de6009f.x: The AMASR Act is of 1958; the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act is of 1972 and ICOMOS was founded in 1965.

n9bc3d0ab22c.s: Which of the following is NOT a principle of the Tribal Panchsheel?
o: Tribes should develop along the lines of their own genius.
Tribal languages should be encouraged and preserved.
Tribal areas should be subjected to maximum administrative control.
Tribal communities should be trained to run their own administration.
n9bc3d0ab22c.x: The Tribal Panchsheel advocated avoiding over-administration, so 'maximum administrative control' is not one of its principles.

n00ac450c19c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Telangana inams legislation?
o: The 1967 extension of the Andhra Inams Act to Telangana was upheld by the High Court.
The Telangana Inams Act was enacted in 1955.
Religious and charitable inams were exempted.
The Act was stalled in courts.
n00ac450c19c.x: The 1967 extension of the Andhra Inams Act to Telangana was struck down, not upheld, by the High Court.

n1577a8b979a.s: With reference to the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, which pair is correctly matched?
o: Chief Minister when the Land Reforms Bill was passed – N.T. Rama Rao
Ceiling per family unit (wet land) – 35-54 acres
Ceiling per family unit (dry land) – 10-27 acres
n1577a8b979a.x: The Act is of 1973, following the Land Reforms Bill under CM P.V. Narasimha Rao; the ceiling was 10-27 acres wet or 35-54 acres dry per family unit.

n612ddf960d7.s: With reference to the Hyderabad (Telangana Area) Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1950, which pair is correctly matched?
o: Purchase price for ownership – 40% of market price
Context of the Act – Telangana armed struggle of 1956-61
Protected tenant with hereditary rights – six years' cultivation
n612ddf960d7.x: Six years' cultivation made a tenant a protected tenant with hereditary rights. Ownership could be bought at 60% of market price in 20 instalments, and the context was the Telangana armed struggle of 1946-51.

n825980de08e.x: Mangroth in Hamirpur, Uttar Pradesh, became the first Gramdan village in 1952; Bhoodan began at Pochampalli.

n53d65c6717e.s: Transfers of land in others' names to defeat ceiling laws are known as:
n53d65c6717e.x: Benami transfers helped defeat the objectives of ceiling laws; oral leases and exemptions also weakened land reforms.

n6238bf3eec6.s: Under the land-ceiling guidelines of 1972, the unit for applying the ceiling was the:
n6238bf3eec6.x: From 1972 the family, not the individual landholder, was made the unit for ceilings.

n5acc41f9dc7.s: Operation Barga (1977), the notable exception to failed tenancy reform, was carried out in:
n5acc41f9dc7.x: Operation Barga (1977) was carried out in West Bengal, not Kerala.

n8649edc3542.s: The Madras Devadasi (Prevention of Dedication) Act of December 1947 was piloted by:
n8649edc3542.x: The Act was piloted by Muthulakshmi Reddy; Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu was a reformer who campaigned against the Bhogam system.

n8faf809ca18.s: The first residential school in Andhra Pradesh (1971) was set up at:
n8faf809ca18.x: The first residential school was set up at Sarvail in Nalgonda district in 1971, under P.V. Narasimha Rao.

n3fee15049d6.s: Which committee of 1949 helped set the agenda for land reform in India?
n3fee15049d6.x: The Kumarappa Committee of 1949 set the land reform agenda; Phase I of land reform covered 1947-70.

n8eec6e9b796.s: The AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956, prescribed a minimum lease period of:
n8eec6e9b796.x: The Act required written lease deeds and leases of at least six years; it came into force in 1961.

ncc19d4d0e43.s: Goa, Daman and Diu were integrated into India through:
ncc19d4d0e43.x: Goa, Daman and Diu were integrated through Operation Vijay; Dadra and Nagar Haveli was freed separately in 1954.

n32501c468bd.s: Backward Muslims in Andhra Pradesh were given a 4% quota under the category:
n32501c468bd.x: Backward Muslims got 4% reservation under BC-E, introduced in 2007.

n89685cda11c.s: Under the planned Andhra Pradesh New Tenancy Act, 2024, tenants get rights over:
o: The land after six years of cultivation
n89685cda11c.x: Tenants get rights on the crop, not the land, along with entitlement cards and access to crop loans.

n3af7a9ab3b9.s: Total prohibition was introduced in Andhra Pradesh under N.T. Rama Rao in:
n3af7a9ab3b9.x: Total prohibition came in 1995, after the Dubagunta movement (1992) and the arrack ban (1993); it was lifted in 1997.

naf3ad7dc012.s: Article 371D, which implemented the Six-Point Formula, was inserted by the:
naf3ad7dc012.x: The Six-Point Formula of 1973 was implemented through Article 371D, inserted by the 32nd Constitutional Amendment in 1973.

n5f163fbac97.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Scheduled Tribe profile (Census 2011)?
o: Odisha has the largest tribal population.
n5f163fbac97.x: Madhya Pradesh, not Odisha, has the largest tribal population; the other three statements are correct.

n0df2225a641.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Dhimsa dance is correctly matched?
o: Position of hands – on one another's waists
n0df2225a641.x: Dhimsa's origin is traced to Koraput. It is danced by groups of about 15-20 women in circles with hands on one another's shoulders.

na853696f553.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the festivals carry no dates)
na853696f553.s: Deepavali is called ____ by the Lambadis.
na853696f553.x: The Lambadis call Deepavali Kalimas; Jari Gundu is another name for Heli Panduga.

nebc365dca8b.s: The Guinness World Record for the largest Dhimsa dance (July 2026) was set at:
o: Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram
nebc365dca8b.x: Over 13,000 tribal women and girl students danced at the Bhogapuram airport in Vizianagaram; the certificate went to the AP Tribal Welfare Department.

n35019cc9b69.s: Who can amend the notified list of Scheduled Tribes under Article 342(2)?
n35019cc9b69.x: Only Parliament can amend the list (Art. 342(2)); the President only notifies it after consulting the Governor.

nindian-polity-1-21.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: First Supreme Court at Fort William – 1774
First Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Fort William – Sir Elijah Impey
First Law Member of the Governor-General's Council – Sir Elijah Impey
Section 87 of the Charter Act, 1833 – opened Company service to Indians without discrimination
nindian-polity-1-21.x: Macaulay, not Sir Elijah Impey, was the first Law Member; Impey was the first Chief Justice at Fort William (1774).

n12cd0482584.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Regulating Act, 1773?
o: It made the Presidencies of Bombay and Madras subordinate to Bengal.
It abolished the Court of Directors.
It was based on the report of a committee under Lord North.
It was the British Parliament's first step to control the East India Company.
n12cd0482584.x: The Regulating Act did not abolish the Court of Directors, which survived until the 1858 Act.

n8921fafe840.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Indians' share in administration?
o: The Charter Act of 1833 said no Indian would be debarred from office by religion, birth, descent or colour.
The Charter Act of 1853 introduced open competition for the civil services.
The Macaulay Committee (1854) was set up to give effect to open competition.
The Charter Act of 1833 put open competition into actual operation.
n8921fafe840.x: The 1833 Act only attempted open competition, which was not implemented; open competition came with the 1853 Act.

nindian-polity-22-61.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Indian Councils Act, 1909 – Transferred rule from the Company to the Crown
Government of India Act, 1919 – Bicameralism at the Centre
Government of India Act, 1935 – Federal Court (1937)
Government of India Act, 1858 – Transferred rule from the Company to the Crown
nindian-polity-22-61.x: The 1909 Act introduced separate electorates for Muslims; it was the 1858 Act that transferred rule to the Crown.

n8deab8e3fc1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Governor's address to a provincial/State legislature?
o: Section 63 of the GoI Act, 1935 dealt with the Governor's address.
Provincial ministries drafted the speech from April 1937.
Article 175 makes the Governor's address absolutely mandatory in every circumstance.
Article 175 of the Constitution provides for the Governor's address.
n8deab8e3fc1.x: Article 175 provides for the Governor's address, but does not make it mandatory in every circumstance.

nindian-polity-22-31.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Satyendra Prasad Sinha – First Indian on the Viceroy's Executive Council
Government of India Act, 1919 – Chamber of Princes
Government of India Act, 1935 – Maurice Gwyer as Chief Justice of the Federal Court
Indian Councils Act, 1909 – Established the Chamber of Princes
nindian-polity-22-31.x: The Chamber of Princes was set up under the 1919 Act; the 1909 Act allowed supplementary questions.

n7309bca1b62.s: The Charter Act of 1833, the final step towards centralisation, made the East India Company:
o: A Crown department under the India Office
A trading body with its monopoly restored
n7309bca1b62.x: The 1833 Act ended the Company's commercial functions and made it purely administrative, while centralising legislation in the Governor-General-in-Council.

nd24c1584728.s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1861, an ordinance issued by the Viceroy could remain in force for at most:
nd24c1584728.x: An ordinance under the 1861 Act lasted at most six months, not twelve.

ne643f048b2b.s: Responsible governments in the provinces under the Government of India Act, 1935 came into force from:
ne643f048b2b.x: The 1935 Act abolished provincial dyarchy, and ministries answerable to the legislatures took office from April 1937.

n60f72cc2a4b.s: How many legislative members did the Charter Act of 1853 add to the Governor-General's Council?
n60f72cc2a4b.x: The 1853 Act added six legislative members, separating legislative from executive functions of the Council.

nindian-polity-1-24.s: Who is known as the 'Father of Communal Electorate'?
nindian-polity-1-24.x: Lord Minto, of the Morley-Minto reforms (Indian Councils Act, 1909), which introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

nindian-polity-1-27.s: The first Chief Justice of the Federal Court (inaugurated on 1 October 1937) was:
nindian-polity-1-27.x: Sir Maurice Gwyer was the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court, which the Supreme Court replaced in 1950.

n08577211175.s: The office of the High Commissioner for India in London was created by the:
n08577211175.x: The 1919 Act provided for a High Commissioner for India in London, a Public Service Commission and separate provincial budgets.

n62057d4fb55.s: The All India Federation proposed by the Government of India Act, 1935 never came into existence because:
o: The Federal Court declared it invalid
n62057d4fb55.x: Accession of the princely states was optional, and since no princely state joined, the Federation never came into operation.

ne94193dce33.s: The Simon Commission, chaired by Sir John Simon, was appointed in:
ne94193dce33.x: The Simon Commission was appointed in 1927, two years before the scheduled review; all seven members were British and it was boycotted in India.

nindian-polity-43-39.s: Which Act provided an annual grant of Rs 1 lakh for education in India?
nindian-polity-43-39.x: The Charter Act of 1813 provided the annual education grant of Rs 1 lakh.

nc3bbd12defc.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, the central legislature was to consist of the Federal Assembly and the:
nc3bbd12defc.x: The 1935 Act's bicameral Centre was the Federal Assembly plus the Council of States; communal representation was also extended to depressed classes, women and labour.

nindian-polity-43-23.s: Provincial autonomy was introduced by the:
nindian-polity-43-23.x: The 1935 Act introduced provincial autonomy; the 1919 Act had introduced dyarchy in the provinces.

nc1286dc818d.s: Dyarchy in the provinces was introduced by the:
nc1286dc818d.x: Provincial dyarchy came with the 1919 Act; provincial autonomy and the proposed central dyarchy belonged to the 1935 Act.

n14fb65bdd0a.s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1909, the additional members of the Central Legislative Council were raised to:
n14fb65bdd0a.x: The 1909 Act raised the additional members to 60 (total 69), though the Centre kept an official majority.

n71d595c1b39.s: Which provision of the Government of India Act, 1935 was never implemented?
o: Federal and Provincial Public Service Commissions
n71d595c1b39.x: Dyarchy at the Centre was never implemented because the Federation did not come into operation; provincial autonomy and the Federal Court were implemented.

n6763e97a1c4.s: The Reserve Bank of India was formed on 1 April 1935 under the:
n6763e97a1c4.x: The 1935 Act provided for the RBI, but the bank was formed on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934.

nindian-polity-22-13.x: Pitt's India Act, 1784 introduced Dual Control; the Regulating Act set up the Supreme Court at Calcutta.

n298d4b95a13.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1858, the Crown's powers over India were exercised through the:
n298d4b95a13.x: The 1858 Act vested the Crown's powers in the Secretary of State for India, assisted by a 15-member Council of India; the Board of Control and Court of Directors were abolished.

nf6d9eb3849c.s: Under the Charter Act of 1793, the salaries of the Board of Control were charged to:
nf6d9eb3849c.x: The Charter Act of 1793 charged the Board of Control's salaries to Indian revenues and increased the Governor-General's control over Bombay and Madras.

n6aa163d0dd3.s: The Governor-General's power to override his Council was first given to Lord Cornwallis by the Act of:
n6aa163d0dd3.x: The Act of 1786 gave the override power to Cornwallis; the Charter Act of 1793 extended it to all future Governors-General and Presidency Governors.

nef6891bd31d.s: Montagu's declaration on the gradual introduction of responsible government in India was made on 20 August:
nef6891bd31d.x: Montagu's declaration of 20 August 1917 formed the basis of the Government of India Act, 1919.

ne48cbf7b2d0.s: Pitt's India Act, 1784 described the Company's territories in India as:
ne48cbf7b2d0.x: The Act described the territories as British possessions in India and made the Company subordinate to the State.

n74214746fc9.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, Defence and Foreign Affairs were:
o: Federal subjects under the federal legislature
n74214746fc9.x: Defence and foreign affairs were reserved subjects under the Governor-General, not the federal legislature.

nfbd01009858.s: Under the Regulating Act, 1773, the Governor-General of Bengal was assisted by an Executive Council of:
nfbd01009858.x: The Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings) had a four-member Executive Council; Pitt's India Act later reduced it to three.

nd936f6aa2fb.s: The principle of indirect election was introduced by the Indian Councils Act of:
nd936f6aa2fb.x: Indirect election began with the 1892 Act; nomination of Indians began in 1861 and separate electorates in 1909.

n051038d44e3.s: The Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774) initially had one Chief Justice and how many other judges?
n051038d44e3.x: It had one Chief Justice (Sir Elijah Impey) and three other judges.

n85c822fa315.s: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly except in:
n85c822fa315.x: The 1813 Act did not end the monopoly completely: tea and the China trade remained exceptions. It also permitted missionaries to enter India.

nindian-polity-1-42.s: The Public Accounts Committee was first set up in:
nindian-polity-1-42.x: The PAC was first set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919.

n0e80025ea17.s: The Act of 1767 required the East India Company to pay the British Government an annual sum of:
n0e80025ea17.x: The Act of 1767 fixed an annual payment of £400,000.

nd95f217adb6.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1919, the upper house of the central legislature was the:
nd95f217adb6.x: The 1919 Act made the Centre bicameral: the Council of State (upper) and the Legislative Assembly (lower).

nindian-polity-43-20.s: Under the Dual Control set up by Pitt's India Act, 1784, political affairs were assigned to the:
nindian-polity-43-20.x: Dual Control gave political functions to the Board of Control and commercial functions to the Court of Directors.

n3c47e449bc2.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Constituent Assembly is wrongly matched?
o: Adoption of the National Flag – 22 July 1947
Adoption of the Munshi-Ayyangar formula – 14 September 1949
Election of Rajendra Prasad as first President – 24 January 1950
n3c47e449bc2.x: Commonwealth membership was ratified in May 1949; 14 September 1949 is when the Munshi-Ayyangar formula was adopted.

ndbf048de4a8.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Constituent Assembly is wrongly matched?
o: Speaker when sitting as Dominion Legislature – G.V. Mavalankar
ndbf048de4a8.x: The Constitutional Adviser was B.N. Rau; Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary President.

ncc818aafcd9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the constitutional position of national symbols?
o: Article 51A(a) refers to respect for the National Flag and the National Anthem.
Article 51A(a) is part of the Fundamental Duties.
Article 51A(a) expressly names the National Song along with the Flag and the Anthem.
A 2026 amendment gave the National Song statutory protection comparable to the Anthem.
ncc818aafcd9.x: Article 51A(a) names the National Flag and the National Anthem, not the National Song.

nindian-polity-5-9.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the demand for a Constituent Assembly is wrongly matched?
o: Swaraj Party – First formal demand at Ranchi, May 1934
Congress – Official demand for the first time in 1935
Jawaharlal Nehru – Accepted the principle of a Constituent Assembly in 1940
August Offer – Accepted the principle of a Constituent Assembly in 1940
nindian-polity-5-9.x: Nehru's clear statement supporting a Constituent Assembly came in 1938; it was the August Offer of 1940 that accepted the principle.

n1d5aa8cefd0.s: Which of the following remarks on the Constituent Assembly is wrongly matched with its author?
o: Represented "only one major community" – Winston Churchill
"A one-party body in an essentially one-party country" – Granville Austin
n1d5aa8cefd0.x: Viscount Simon, not Granville Austin, called the Assembly "a body of Hindus".

nc1c4b93061e.s: Which of the following pairs of date and Constituent Assembly event is wrongly matched?
o: 17 November 1947 – Assembly met as Dominion Legislature
nc1c4b93061e.x: On 22 January 1947 the Objectives Resolution was adopted; the Draft Constitution was published on 21 February 1948.

na57c645514f.s: The representatives of the princely States in the Constituent Assembly were:
o: Elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies
na57c645514f.x: Princely representatives were nominated by the rulers; only the provincial members were elected by the Provincial Assemblies.

nbf7ba5067ba.s: Constitution Day (26 November) has been observed since:
nbf7ba5067ba.x: Constitution Day has been observed since 2015, the 125th birth-anniversary year of B.R. Ambedkar.

nb3f3a08d354.s: In the Interim Government of 1946, Liaquat Ali Khan held the portfolio of:
nb3f3a08d354.x: Liaquat Ali Khan held Finance; Home (with Information and Broadcasting) was with Sardar Patel and Food and Agriculture with Rajendra Prasad.

nindian-polity-52-21.s: The Union Powers Committee of the Constituent Assembly dealt with:
nindian-polity-52-21.x: The Union Powers Committee handled the distribution of federal subjects; the Order of Business Committee handled the daily agenda.

n53d87199a0b.s: Which of the following provisions came into force on 26 November 1949?
n53d87199a0b.x: Citizenship, elections, the provisional Parliament and transitional provisions came into force on 26 November 1949; the rest commenced on 26 January 1950.

n6314fe97e55.s: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, the total strength of the Constituent Assembly was to be:
n6314fe97e55.x: The total strength was 389: 296 from British India and 93 from the princely states.

nd46c30c4486.s: Under the Instrument of Accession (1947), a princely state ceded defence, external affairs and ____ to the Dominion.
nd46c30c4486.x: The Instrument of Accession ceded defence, external affairs and communications, not finance.

nindian-polity-1-30.s: Who first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India in 1934?
nindian-polity-1-30.x: M.N. Roy first put forward the idea in 1934; the Swaraj Party made the first formal demand at Ranchi in May 1934.

n3e840e06064.s: The Minorities Sub-committee of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by:
n3e840e06064.x: H.C. Mukherjee chaired the Minorities Sub-committee; Kripalani chaired the Fundamental Rights Sub-committee.

nindian-polity-5-4.s: The Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal Areas was chaired by:
nindian-polity-5-4.x: Sardar Patel chaired the Advisory Committee; J.B. Kripalani chaired the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee.

ne7aa1ee7995.s: The Constituent Assembly sat for a total of:
ne7aa1ee7995.x: The Assembly held 11 sessions over 165 days; the Draft Constitution alone was discussed for 114 days.

n2d64672f28d.s: After independence, the Governor-General of each Dominion was to act on the advice of the:
n2d64672f28d.x: The Governor-General, common or separate for each Dominion, was to act on the advice of the Dominion ministers.

nf47ebcd9dab.s: The Constituent Assembly took about how long to complete its work?
nf47ebcd9dab.x: The Assembly took about three years, for which it was criticised, along with not being based on adult franchise.

nf88a5f4bbc0.s: The Objectives Resolution, moved by Nehru on 13 December 1946, was adopted on:
nf88a5f4bbc0.x: The Objectives Resolution was unanimously adopted on 22 January 1947; 26 November 1949 is when the Constitution was adopted.

n7b2336e2bc0.s: The Draft Constitution initially contained how many Articles?
n7b2336e2bc0.x: The Draft had 315 Articles; 395 Articles belong to the adopted text.

nc88bf2fcd11.s: How many of the 299 members signed the Constitution on 24 January 1950?
nc88bf2fcd11.x: 284 of the 299 members signed the Constitution at the final session on 24 January 1950.

n31814ac1fd3.s: Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected President of the Constituent Assembly on:
n31814ac1fd3.x: Prasad was elected on 11 December 1946, not at the first meeting, which was attended by 211 members and boycotted by the Muslim League.

nindian-polity-5-7.s: The ad-hoc Flag Committee of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by:
nindian-polity-5-7.x: Dr Rajendra Prasad chaired the Flag Committee, the Steering Committee and the Rules of Procedure Committee; Nehru chaired the Union Powers Committee.

nba56db116f2.s: The Constituent Assembly of India was:
o: Wholly nominated by the British Government
Wholly nominated by the princely rulers
nba56db116f2.x: The Assembly was partly elected and partly nominated; it was not based on adult franchise.

ndcdd7f558cd.s: The Drafting Committee, chaired by Dr B.R. Ambedkar, sat for:
ndcdd7f558cd.x: The seven-member Drafting Committee chaired by Ambedkar sat for 141 days.

nindian-polity-35-14.s: Who chaired both the Union Constitution Committee and the Union Powers Committee?
nindian-polity-35-14.x: Nehru chaired both committees, which dealt with the Union's structure and the division of legislative power.

n0834d21b049.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about features borrowed from Australia and the USSR?
o: The ideals of social, economic and political justice in the Preamble came from Australia.
The Concurrent List came from Australia.
Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse came from Australia.
Fundamental Duties came from the USSR.
n0834d21b049.x: The ideals of social, economic and political justice in the Preamble were borrowed from the USSR, not Australia.

n1d7738bdeec.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about borrowed features of the Constitution?
o: Residuary powers with the Centre came from South Africa.
The method of election of the President came from Ireland.
Nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha came from Ireland.
Election of Rajya Sabha members and the amendment procedure came from South Africa.
n1d7738bdeec.x: Residuary powers with the Centre were borrowed from Canada, not South Africa.

n6b7af0236f5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about residuary powers?
o: In India, residuary powers lie exclusively with the States.
In India, residuary powers lie with Parliament under Article 248.
In the USA and Australia, residuary powers lie with the States.
India's arrangement of residuary powers was borrowed from Canada.
n6b7af0236f5.x: In India residuary powers lie with Parliament (Article 248), following the Canadian model.

n6db31abb04d.s: Suspension of Fundamental Rights during an Emergency is a feature associated with:
n6db31abb04d.x: Suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency is associated with Weimar Germany; the general emergency scheme is associated with the 1935 Act.

na00f8b5559b.s: Ireland, from which India took the Directive Principles, had itself taken the idea from:
na00f8b5559b.x: Ireland took the idea of Directive Principles from Spain; India adapted it as a novel feature of its Constitution.

nd685d15457b.s: India borrowed the parliamentary system and its conventions from:
nd685d15457b.x: The parliamentary system and its conventions came from Britain, even though Britain has no single written Constitution.

n31ec1b1c93c.s: A joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament under Article 108 is presided over by the:
o: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
n31ec1b1c93c.x: A joint sitting under Article 108, itself an Australian borrowing, is presided over by the Speaker.

nindian-polity-3-1.s: The idea of a federation with a strong Centre was borrowed from:
nindian-polity-3-1.x: A federation with a strong Centre came from Canada; the Concurrent List came from Australia.

n4eed3f31ac5.s: Single citizenship in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
n4eed3f31ac5.x: Single citizenship, like bicameralism and the cabinet system, came from Britain; the USA has dual citizenship.

nd57d10c4b60.s: The eleventh Fundamental Duty was added by the:
nd57d10c4b60.x: Fundamental Duties were introduced by the 42nd Amendment (1976); the eleventh duty was added by the 86th Amendment.

nindian-polity-3-4.s: The idea of the Preamble in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
nindian-polity-3-4.x: The idea of the Preamble came from the USA; France gave liberty, equality, fraternity and the Republic.

nindian-polity-3-5.s: The language of the Preamble was borrowed from the Constitution of:
nindian-polity-3-5.x: The language of the Preamble came from Australia, while the GoI Act, 1935 gave the Constitution its structural and administrative backbone.

nindian-polity-3-11.s: The provision for a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament was borrowed from:
nindian-polity-3-11.x: The joint sitting, freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse, and the language of the Preamble came from Australia.

nindian-polity-3-13.s: The ideal of a Republic in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
nindian-polity-3-13.x: The ideal of a Republic, like liberty, equality and fraternity, was borrowed from France.

n9f80135bf2d.s: A system in which a single hierarchy of courts enforces both Central and State laws is called:
n9f80135bf2d.x: India has an integrated judiciary with one hierarchy of courts for both Central and State laws, unlike the separate federal and State courts of the USA.

n511245fbe8a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: States in the United States have their own constitutions.
The United States has dual citizenship.
Indian States do not have separate constitutions of their own.
n511245fbe8a.x: Indian States have neither separate constitutions nor dual citizenship; the United States has both.

nf7471c7ac41.s: Which of the following is NOT a reason for the large size of the Indian Constitution?
o: The size and diversity of India
The influence of the Government of India Act, 1935
The dominance of legal luminaries in the Constituent Assembly
nf7471c7ac41.x: The Constitution is long partly because it includes detailed administrative provisions, so 'exclusion of administrative details' is wrong.

n6974eb8880f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Indian and British parliamentary systems?
o: India's head of state is elected.
The Indian Parliament is sovereign in the British sense.
The British system rests on the sovereignty of Parliament.
The Indian Parliament is bound by a written Constitution and judicial review.
n6974eb8880f.x: The Indian Parliament is not sovereign in the British sense: it is bound by a written Constitution, Fundamental Rights and judicial review.

n4efbe1ada9f.s:
Assertion (A): The Indian Constitution establishes a religious state.
Reason (R): India has no state religion.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n4efbe1ada9f.x: A is false: India is a secular state. R is true: India has no state religion.

n0dad1c0affe.s: The emergency provisions (Articles 352-360) are contained in:
n0dad1c0affe.x: Part XVIII (Arts. 352-360) provides for National, State (President's Rule) and Financial Emergencies.

n9dea8a330b1.s: India follows which form of democracy?
o: Direct democracy through referendum and recall
n9dea8a330b1.x: India follows representative or indirect democracy; referendum, initiative and recall are not part of its national system.

n500883732c9.s: In India, both Central and State laws are enforced by:
o: Separate federal and State court systems
n500883732c9.x: India has an integrated judiciary in which one court system administers both Union and State laws.

n9dd82955e03.s: Judicial review in India is narrower than in the USA because Article 21 uses the phrase:
n9dd82955e03.x: Article 21 uses 'procedure established by law', which makes judicial review in India narrower than in the USA.

nfccdb21f4ef.s: The original Constitution of India contained how many Schedules?
nfccdb21f4ef.x: The original Constitution had 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules; there are 12 Schedules now.

n165749a6e09.s: Which doctrine limits the amending power of the Indian Parliament?
n165749a6e09.x: Parliament is a creature of the Constitution, and its amending power is limited by the basic structure doctrine.

n90575ca5c55.s: Part IXB was added to the Constitution by the:
n90575ca5c55.x: Part IXB was added by the 97th Amendment in 2011; Part IXA came by the 74th Amendment in 1992.

n0275f2b6c15.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the objectives in the Preamble?
o: Economic justice means removing economic discrimination and glaring inequality.
Liberty means the complete absence of every restraint on individual activity.
Political justice means equal political rights and access to office.
Equality has civic, political and economic dimensions.
n0275f2b6c15.x: Liberty means absence of restraints plus opportunities to develop one's personality, not freedom from every restraint.

n3214c5c8742.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the terms in the Preamble?
o: 'Socialist' denotes democratic socialism with public and private sectors co-existing.
Indian socialism is a blend of Marxism and Gandhism.
Indian socialism leans towards Gandhian socialism.
'Democratic' in the Preamble is a mix of British Fabian Socialism and American Populism.
n3214c5c8742.x: Describing 'Democratic' as a mix of Fabian Socialism and American Populism is not valid; the APPSC G1 2024 key treated it as wrong.

n191f2bac169.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the terms used in the Preamble?
o: 'Democratic' covers political, social and economic democracy.
'Republic' means the head of state is elected.
'Republic' means no public office is hereditary.
n191f2bac169.x: 'Democratic' is not limited to political democracy; it covers social and economic democracy as well.

nindian-polity-14-2.s: Which of the following pairs of Preamble term and meaning is wrongly matched?
o: Sovereign – Supreme authority, free from external control
Socialist – Head of the State is elected
Republic – Head of the State is elected
Fraternity – Dignity of the individual and unity and integrity of the Nation
nindian-polity-14-2.x: 'Socialist' aims at reducing inequality; an elected head of State is the meaning of 'Republic'.

nindian-polity-14-11.s: In the Indian context, secularism means:
o: A State religion with tolerance of others
nindian-polity-14-11.x: Secularism in India means equal respect for all religions.

nfb6351cf74e.s: In which case did the Supreme Court call the Preamble a key to the minds of the framers?
nfb6351cf74e.x: Berubari called the Preamble a key to the framers' minds; though non-justiciable, it is an aid to interpreting ambiguous provisions.

nc43950c2645.s: A secular State in the Indian constitutional sense is one that:
o: Is hostile to all religious practices
Has an official religion but tolerates others
nc43950c2645.x: A secular State has no State religion and gives equal respect to all religions; it is not hostile to religion.

n80d918de94e.s: The idea of Fraternity in the Preamble is possibly drawn from which Article of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
n80d918de94e.x: Fraternity, a sense of brotherhood promoted by single citizenship, is possibly drawn from Article 1 of the UDHR (1948), not Article 29.

n88f3fa41185.s: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 was enacted during the Emergency under the leadership of:
n88f3fa41185.x: The 42nd Amendment was enacted during the Emergency of 1975-77 under Indira Gandhi.

ncfc8e6bbbad.s: Which of these words in the Preamble was in the original 1949 text and was NOT added by the 42nd Amendment?
ncfc8e6bbbad.x: The 42nd Amendment added Socialist, Secular and Integrity; Fraternity was in the original 1949 text.

n2d6d483a031.s: Which of the following expressions is found in the Preamble?
n2d6d483a031.x: 'Dignity of the individual' is in the Preamble (fraternity assuring it); 'Federal', 'Fundamental Duties' and 'adult franchise' are not.

n96addc89ca3.s: The 42nd Amendment's clauses giving Parliament unlimited amending power and excluding judicial review were struck down in:
n96addc89ca3.x: Those clauses of the 'Mini-Constitution' were struck down in Minerva Mills (1980); Kesavananda Bharati came before the 1976 amendment.

n878382d6dc6.s: Who called the Preamble the 'political horoscope' of the Constitution?
n878382d6dc6.x: K.M. Munshi called it the 'political horoscope'; Palkhivala called it the 'identity card' and Thakurdas Bhargava the 'soul'.

nindian-polity-14-5.s: The date mentioned in the Preamble is:

nindian-polity-14-12.s: According to the Preamble, the Constitution was given to the people of India by:
nindian-polity-14-12.x: The Preamble says 'We, the people of India ... give to ourselves this Constitution', so the people are its source.

nindian-polity-14-18.s: The Preamble reflects the philosophy, the ideals and the ____ of the Constitution.
nindian-polity-14-18.x: The Preamble reflects the philosophy, ideals and objectives of the Constitution.

nindian-polity-14-8.s: Which case held that the Preamble is part of the Constitution and can be amended, but its basic structure cannot be destroyed?
nindian-polity-14-8.x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held the Preamble is part of the Constitution and amendable under Article 368, but its basic structure cannot be destroyed.

nindian-polity-14-7.s: The Golaknath case was decided in:
nindian-polity-14-7.x: Golaknath was decided in 1967, after Berubari (1960) and before Kesavananda Bharati (1973) and LIC of India (1995).

n9275e52683b.s: The 42nd Amendment inserted 'Socialist' and 'Secular' into the Preamble between the words:
n9275e52683b.x: They were inserted between 'Sovereign' and 'Democratic', so the Preamble now reads 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic'.

nindian-polity-48-19.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Article 371-B – Committee of Assembly members from tribal areas (Assam)
Article 371-C – Committee of Assembly members from tribal areas (Assam)
Article 371-F – Special provisions on incorporation and governance (Sikkim)
Article 371-J – Special development board and reservations (Hyderabad-Karnataka)
nindian-polity-48-19.x: Article 371-C provides Manipur's committee of members elected from the Hill areas; the Assam tribal-area committee is under 371-B.

nindian-polity-5-2-6.s: Which of the following pairs of Schedule and subject is wrongly matched?
o: Second Schedule – Emoluments and privileges of constitutional authorities
Third Schedule – Forms of oaths and affirmations
Fifth Schedule – Tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
Sixth Schedule – Tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
nindian-polity-5-2-6.x: The Fifth Schedule deals with Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes; the tribal areas of the four north-eastern States are in the Sixth Schedule.

nindian-polity-6-17.s: Which of the following pairs of Part and subject is wrongly matched?
o: Part XVI – Special provisions relating to certain classes
nindian-polity-6-17.x: Part XVII (Articles 343-351) deals with the Official Language; Emergency provisions are in Part XVIII.

nindian-polity-5-2-4.s: Which of the following pairs of Schedule and subject is wrongly matched?
o: First Schedule – Names and territories of States and UTs
Seventh Schedule – Union, State and Concurrent Lists
nindian-polity-5-2-4.x: The Fourth Schedule allocates Rajya Sabha seats; the anti-defection law is in the Tenth Schedule.

nindian-polity-2-56.s: Which of the following pairs of Articles and subject is wrongly matched?
nindian-polity-2-56.x: Articles 330-334 deal with reservation of seats for SCs, STs and Anglo-Indians; the Official Language is in Articles 343-351.

nindian-polity-6-10.s: Part VII of the Constitution (Part B States) was repealed by the:
nindian-polity-6-10.x: Part VII was repealed by the 7th Amendment (1956).

nindian-polity-6-14.s: Part XIV-A of the Constitution deals with:
o: Services under the Union and the States
Special provisions relating to certain classes
nindian-polity-6-14.x: Part XIV-A (Articles 323A-323B) deals with Tribunals; Part XIV covers Services and Part XV Elections.

nindian-polity-2-67.s: Article 338B of the Constitution deals with the:
nindian-polity-2-67.x: Article 338B provides for the National Commission for Backward Classes; 338A is for Scheduled Tribes.

na586ab563ad.s: Part II of the Constitution deals with:
na586ab563ad.x: Part II concerns citizenship; Part I covers the Union and its territory.

n182fac192cc.s: Part IX-A of the Constitution, dealing with the Municipalities, was added by the:
n182fac192cc.x: Part IX-A came by the 74th Amendment, 1992; the 73rd added Part IX and the 97th added Part IX-B.

n2a9a5a49a38.s: The forms of oaths and affirmations are contained in the:
n2a9a5a49a38.x: Oaths and affirmations are in the Third Schedule; the Seventh Schedule has the Union, State and Concurrent Lists.

nee8261b7079.s: The Ninth Schedule of the Constitution is linked with Article:
nee8261b7079.x: The Ninth Schedule, which originally had 13 Acts, is connected with Article 31B.

n87a47f16cc8.s: Part IX-B of the Constitution deals with:
n87a47f16cc8.x: Part IX-B concerns co-operative societies; Part IX covers Panchayats and Part IX-A Municipalities.

n11dfc19ae13.s: The Ninth Schedule, the first Schedule added to the Constitution, was inserted by the:
n11dfc19ae13.x: The Ninth Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment, 1951; the Constitution had 8 Schedules originally and has 12 now.

nd228498b82a.s: Article 1 of the Constitution declares 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a':
nd228498b82a.x: Article 1 calls India a Union of States; States have no right to secede.

nindian-polity-2-16.s: The Finance Commission is provided for under Article:
nindian-polity-2-16.x: The Finance Commission is under Article 280; the Election Commission is under Article 324.

n8b574fb5479.s: Part XIV-A (Tribunals) was added to the Constitution by the:
n8b574fb5479.x: Part XIV-A was added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976, which also added Part IV-A, not by the 44th.

nfd2f733ad0c.s: The Vice-President takes the oath of office under:
nfd2f733ad0c.x: The Vice-President takes an oath under Article 69, not under the Third Schedule, which has oaths for State legislators and High Court judges.

nindian-polity-48-5.x: Article 371-A covers Nagaland; 371-B Assam, 371-C Manipur and 371-D Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

nindian-polity-6-7.s: Part IV of the Constitution (Directive Principles) covers Articles:

nindian-polity-6-19.s: Part XX of the Constitution contains Article:
nindian-polity-6-19.x: Part XX contains Article 368 (amendment); Part IV-A contains Article 51-A.

n20032609d0d.s: Special provisions for Maharashtra and Gujarat are contained in Article:
n20032609d0d.x: Article 371 covers Maharashtra and Gujarat; 371A is Nagaland, 371B Assam and 371F Sikkim.

nindian-polity-5-2-5.s: Sindhi was added to the Eighth Schedule by the:
nindian-polity-5-2-5.x: Sindhi came by the 21st Amendment (1967); Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali by the 71st (1992); Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali by the 92nd (2003).

nindian-polity-5-2-3.s: The Ninth Schedule mainly validates and protects laws relating to:
nindian-polity-5-2-3.x: The Ninth Schedule, added by the 1st Amendment (1951), validates listed Acts, mainly land reforms, shielding them from judicial review.

n35eddac65da.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019?
o: It created the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir with a legislature.
It created the Union Territory of Ladakh with a legislature.
It abolished the Legislative Council of Jammu and Kashmir.
It came into effect on 31 October 2019.
n35eddac65da.x: The Act created Ladakh as a Union Territory without a legislature.

n7190478a144.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement?
o: It was implemented through the 100th Constitutional Amendment, 2015.
The amendment altered the First Schedule entries of Assam, West Bengal, Meghalaya and Tripura.
51 Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh and 111 Bangladeshi enclaves came to India.
n7190478a144.x: The numbers are reversed: 111 Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh and 51 came to India.

n36c4564221d.s:
Assertion (A): The cession of Berubari to Pakistan could not be made by an ordinary law under Article 3.
Reason (R): In the Berubari reference (1960), the Supreme Court held that Article 3 does not cover cession of territory.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n36c4564221d.x: Because Article 3 does not cover cession, an Article 368 amendment (the 9th Amendment, 1960) was needed; R explains A.

nc90124cb6cc.x: Goa is associated with the 56th Amendment; Mizoram with the 53rd, Arunachal Pradesh with the 55th and Nagaland with the 13th.

n483c160940e.s: The Ministry of Home Affairs has proposed a new Chapter K under Article 371 for:
n483c160940e.x: The proposed Chapter K under Article 371 is for Ladakh, not Jammu and Kashmir.

nc1e99181752.s: Delhi has a legislature under Article:
nc1e99181752.x: Delhi's legislature is under Article 239AA (69th Amendment, 1991); Puducherry's is under Article 239A.

n0b0c583fce1.s: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 provided for:
n0b0c583fce1.x: The SR Act, 1956 created 14 States and 6 UTs, formed Andhra Pradesh and set up Zonal Councils.

n6c63a88aff8.s: Katchatheevu was transferred to Sri Lanka under agreements of:
n6c63a88aff8.x: Katchatheevu went to Sri Lanka under the 1974-76 agreements, without a constitutional amendment.

n64c805602f8.x: Nagaland became a State in 1963, after Andhra State (1953) and before Haryana (1966) and Sikkim (1975).

nindian-polity-63-10.s: Which of the following pairs relating to loss of citizenship is wrongly matched?
o: Termination – Automatic loss on voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship
Deprivation – Compulsory termination by the Central Government
Renunciation – Compulsory termination by the Central Government
Article 9 – Constitutional basis for loss on acquiring foreign citizenship
nindian-polity-63-10.x: Renunciation is a voluntary surrender by an Indian national; compulsory termination by the Centre is deprivation.

n0a31934c78e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about citizenship by birth?
o: Citizenship by birth is dealt with in Section 3 of the Citizenship Act, 1955.
For a person born in India on or after 3 December 2004, both parents must be Indian citizens.
A person born between 1 July 1987 and 2 December 2004 needed at least one Indian-citizen parent.
From 3 December 2004, one Indian-citizen parent suffices if the other is not an illegal migrant.
n0a31934c78e.x: From 3 December 2004, one Indian-citizen parent is enough if the other is not an illegal migrant; both need not be Indian.

nindian-polity-63-2.s: Which of the following pairs of Article and subject is wrongly matched?
o: Article 5 – Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution
Article 7 – Rights of certain migrants to Pakistan
Article 8 – Persons of Indian origin residing abroad
Article 6 – Rights of certain migrants to Pakistan
nindian-polity-63-2.x: Article 6 covers persons who migrated from Pakistan to India; migrants to Pakistan are under Article 7.

nindian-polity-63-16.s: Which of the following pairs of Article and subject is wrongly matched?
o: Article 10 – Parliament to regulate citizenship by law
Article 9 – Voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship
Article 11 – Parliament to regulate citizenship by law
Article 8 – Persons of Indian origin residing abroad
nindian-polity-63-16.x: Article 10 provides for continuance of citizenship; Parliament's power to regulate citizenship is in Article 11.

na7870dbc040.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Part II of the Constitution?
o: It deals only with persons who were citizens at the commencement of the Constitution.
Article 10 provides for continuance of citizenship, subject to laws made by Parliament.
Article 10 empowers Parliament to regulate acquisition and termination of citizenship.
Article 11 empowers Parliament to regulate citizenship by law.
na7870dbc040.x: Parliament's power to regulate acquisition and termination of citizenship is in Article 11, not Article 10.

n742b36d3e9d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about citizenship by naturalisation under the Citizenship Act, 1955?
o: Ordinary residence of 12 years is required.
The residence period includes the 12 months immediately before applying.
Residence conditions can be waived for distinguished service to science, art, literature or world peace.
No oath of allegiance is required.
n742b36d3e9d.x: Naturalisation does require an oath of allegiance.

n64467a6a6b8.s:
Assertion (A): Section 3 of the Citizenship Act, 1955 deals with citizenship by birth.
Reason (R): Section 7 of the Act deals with citizenship by registration.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n64467a6a6b8.x: Section 3 covers citizenship by birth, so A is true; Section 7 covers incorporation of territory (registration is Section 5), so R is false.

n5e37724927b.s: Mizoram became a State on 20 February 1987 under the:
n5e37724927b.x: Mizoram became a State under the State of Mizoram Act, 1986 and the 53rd Amendment, not the SR Act, 1956.

nf206d826036.s: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 reduced the residence requirement for naturalisation to:
nf206d826036.x: The CAA 2019 reduced the naturalisation residence requirement to five years and gives citizenship effect from the date of entry.

n3d26e68c430.s: Which Constitutional Amendment was enacted following the Berubari Union reference?
n3d26e68c430.x: Berubari held that territory could not be ceded under Article 3 and required an Article 368 amendment, which led to the 9th Amendment, 1960.

nd30d3061e21.s: Deprivation of Indian citizenship by the Central Government applies only to citizens by:
nd30d3061e21.x: The Centre may deprive only citizens by naturalisation, registration or Art. 5(c), on grounds such as fraud, disloyalty or aiding an enemy.

nb357dfcf95d.s: Along with Inner Line Permit areas, which areas are exempted from the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019?
o: Sixth Schedule tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Tripura
nb357dfcf95d.x: The Sixth Schedule tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Tripura and the Inner Line Permit areas are exempt; West Bengal's districts are not.

n7f39eef10a9.s: A person is barred from an OCI card if the person or a parent or grandparent was a citizen of:
n7f39eef10a9.x: Those who are or were, or whose parents or grandparents were, citizens of Pakistan or Bangladesh are barred from OCI.

o: Dual citizenship of the Union and the States
Single citizenship for the Union and the States
Separate citizenship for each Union Territory
n4c6c4aae584.x: India has one citizenship for the Union and the States; the Constitution does not recognise a separate State domicile.

nd439fe4095d.s: An Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder enjoys:
o: The right to vote in Indian elections
Eligibility to contest Lok Sabha elections
nd439fe4095d.x: OCI cardholders are foreign nationals of Indian origin with a lifelong visa facility; they cannot vote as OCI cardholders.

nb7b83c22b86.s: After the merger of Dadra and Nagar Haveli with Daman and Diu (26 January 2020), India has how many Union Territories?
nb7b83c22b86.x: India now has 8 Union Territories after the 2020 merger.

nb8b40264da0.s: The freedoms under Article 19 are available to:
nb8b40264da0.x: Article 19 freedoms, like Articles 15, 16, 29 and 30, are available only to citizens.

nindian-polity-63-17.s: Under Article 6, the permit cut-off date for persons who migrated from Pakistan was:
nindian-polity-63-17.x: Article 6 turns on migration before or after 19 July 1948; 1 March 1947 is the date relevant to Article 7.

n15da1ca81c1.s: Aadhaar is not, by itself, proof of citizenship under which Section of the Aadhaar Act?
n15da1ca81c1.x: Aadhaar establishes identity, but under Section 9 of the Aadhaar Act it is not by itself proof of citizenship.

n268b189b254.s: Which of the following was introduced for OCI services by the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026?
o: Merger of PIO and OCI cards
n268b189b254.x: The 2026 Rules introduced e-OCI cards, a central OCI database and online application and renunciation; the PIO-OCI merger was in 2015.

n5f2e5746f8a.s: The PIO and OCI cards were merged in:
n5f2e5746f8a.x: The PIO-OCI merger took place in 2015; the 2003 amendment introduced OCI registration.

n9b5eaa6e176.s: The current residence period for citizenship by registration of a person of Indian origin is:
n9b5eaa6e176.x: The current residence requirement for registration is 7 years; spouses of Indian citizens are also a registration category.

ne52a36d71fd.s: Which community is NOT among the specified religious communities under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019?
ne52a36d71fd.x: The specified communities are Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi and Christian; Muslims are not included.

n3dc7cd96096.s: Puducherry and Goa are examples of territories that India:
n3dc7cd96096.x: As a sovereign State India may acquire foreign territory by cession, treaty or conquest; Puducherry and Goa are examples of acquired territories.

n5ae40c5f0b0.s: OCI registration and Section 14A were introduced by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act of:
n5ae40c5f0b0.x: The 2003 amendment introduced OCI and Sec. 14A; the 2005 amendment widened OCI and the 2015 amendment merged PIO and OCI.

nindian-polity-63-31.s: A naturalised or registered citizen may be deprived of citizenship if imprisoned within five years of naturalisation or registration for at least:
nindian-polity-63-31.x: Under Section 10, two years' imprisonment within five years of naturalisation or registration is a ground, along with fraud, disloyalty and unlawful trade with an enemy.

nbfc687366d8.s: Which of the following pairs relating to 'State' under Article 12 is wrongly matched?
o: Rajasthan SEB v. Mohan Lal (1967) – Statutory bodies are 'other authorities'
Pradeep Kumar Biswas – Financial, functional and administrative domination test
R.D. Shetty v. International Airport Authority – Statutory bodies are 'other authorities'
nbfc687366d8.x: R.D. Shetty (1979) laid down the tests for an instrumentality or agency of the State; the 'other authorities' holding is Rajasthan SEB (1967).

n79471b49dc2.s: Which of the following pairs of Article and provision is wrongly matched?
o: Article 33 – Restriction of Fundamental Rights of specified forces
Article 34 – Restriction of Fundamental Rights of specified forces
Article 35 – Parliament's exclusive power to legislate on specified Part III matters
Article 359 – President's order suspending enforcement of specified rights
n79471b49dc2.x: Article 34 concerns restrictions during martial law and indemnity by Parliament; the forces provision is Article 33.

nc9657ec54a8.s: Which of the following pairs of doctrine and meaning is wrongly matched?
o: Severability – Only the inconsistent portion of a law is void
Waiver – A person cannot give up a Fundamental Right
Prospective overruling – Ruling operates only for the future
Eclipse – Only the inconsistent portion of a law is void
nc9657ec54a8.x: Eclipse means an inconsistent law stays dormant and may revive; voiding only the inconsistent portion is severability.

n180c8d03fa4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about 'State' under Article 12?
o: It includes the Government and Parliament of India.
It includes the Government and Legislature of each State.
It includes other authorities in India or under the control of the Government of India.
n180c8d03fa4.x: Article 12 includes all local authorities within 'State'.

n7b6419927f6.s: The Fundamental Rights chapter of the Indian Constitution was modelled principally on the:
n7b6419927f6.x: The model for the Fundamental Rights is the US Bill of Rights, not the Irish Constitution.

n5f06104fe66.s: Enemy aliens are excluded from the safeguards of Article 22 by its clause:
n5f06104fe66.x: Article 22(3) excludes enemy aliens from the specified safeguards; Articles 23 and 24 are not denied to aliens.

n804cfd4f032.s: Under Article 33, the power to restrict the Fundamental Rights of members of the armed forces lies with:
n804cfd4f032.x: Article 33 gives the power exclusively to Parliament, and it may extend to non-combatant employees such as cooks and barbers.

n00969d95e0e.s: 'Equal pay for equal work' is a constitutional goal under Article:
n00969d95e0e.x: Equal pay for equal work is under Article 39(d); property is protected under Article 300A.

n5256274c1e9.s: Paying labourers less than the minimum wage violates Article:
n5256274c1e9.x: Paying less than minimum wage is forced labour under Art. 23 (PUDR/Asiad, 1982); child labour in mines violates Art. 24.

o: Absolute and cannot be regulated by law
Qualified and subject to reasonable restrictions
n6cd3ac15e37.x: Fundamental Rights are qualified, not absolute; courts review restrictions for reasonableness.

n57c1ae9d039.s: Which 2007 decision limited the protection given by the Ninth Schedule?
n57c1ae9d039.x: I.R. Coelho (2007) limited Ninth Schedule protection; the Schedule itself came with the 1st Amendment (1951).

n72588981b63.s: The right to freedom of religion is contained in Articles:
n72588981b63.x: Freedom of religion is in Articles 25-28; equality is 14-18, exploitation 23-24 and cultural and educational rights 29-30.

nindian-society-45-8.s: Which of the following pairs of case and holding is wrongly matched?
o: Orissa Mining Corp. v. MoEF – Gram Sabha safeguards Dongria Kondh rights
Indra Sawhney – 27% OBC quota and creamy layer exclusion
Janki Prasad Parimoo – Caste alone cannot be the sole determinant of backwardness
Samatha – Caste alone cannot be the sole determinant of backwardness
nindian-society-45-8.x: Samatha held that tribal land cannot be leased to private parties or corporations; the caste holding is Janki Prasad Parimoo.

nindian-society-45-3.s: Which of the following pairs of case and year is wrongly matched?
o: Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta – 2006
Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh – 1997
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India – 2006
State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh – 2024
nindian-society-45-3.x: Jarnail Singh was decided in 2018; 2006 is M. Nagaraj.

n6de4ca2f41c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about titles under Article 18?
o: A non-citizen holding an office of profit or trust under the State needs the President's consent to accept a foreign title.
A citizen of India may accept a foreign title with the President's consent.
A holder of an office of profit or trust needs the President's consent to accept any present from a foreign State.
Bharat Ratna and Padma awards are not titles under Article 18.
n6de4ca2f41c.x: Under Art. 18(2) a citizen shall not accept a foreign title at all; there is no consent route.

nfc993e6c5d0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about prohibited grounds of discrimination?
o: Religion and race are prohibited grounds under Article 15(1).
Caste and sex are prohibited grounds under Article 15(1).
Descent is a prohibited ground under Article 15(1).
Descent is a prohibited ground under Article 16(2).
nfc993e6c5d0.x: Article 15(1) covers only religion, race, caste, sex and place of birth; descent appears in Article 16(2).

nae2b067646d.s: Which of the following is NOT a recognised exception or qualification to the 50% reservation ceiling?
o: Every reservation made by a State legislature, without limitation
Extraordinary situations such as remote areas
Carry-forward of backlog vacancies under the 81st Amendment
EWS reservation upheld in Janhit Abhiyan
nae2b067646d.x: There is no unrestricted power for every State legislature to exceed the ceiling.

ne8fe0d7294d.s: Which of the following pairs of Article and subject is wrongly matched?
o: Article 15(4) – Special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs
Article 340 – Commission on conditions of SEBCs
ne8fe0d7294d.x: Article 16(4A) concerns reservation in promotion for SCs and STs with consequential seniority; backlog vacancies are under 16(4B).

nfbc370a9856.s: A civil case against the President or a Governor can be instituted only after prior notice of:
nfbc370a9856.x: A civil case needs two months' prior notice, not six; criminal proceedings are barred during the term (Art. 361).

o: Caste not being the sole test of backwardness
n06134682da7.x: Champakam Dorairajan concerned the Madras Communal G.O.; M.R. Balaji dealt with caste as sole test and the 50% principle.

nbfb05169107.s: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024), decided by a 7-judge bench, overruled:
nbfb05169107.x: The 7-judge bench overruled E.V. Chinnaiah (2004) and allowed sub-classification of SCs and STs based on empirical data.

n006c7af6f39.s: Which case held that caste cannot be the sole test of backwardness and that reservation should generally stay below 50%?
o: M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India
n006c7af6f39.x: M.R. Balaji held that caste cannot be the sole test and reservation should generally remain below 50%, and must be reasonable.

nfc1dc20ae42.s: Which case required quantifiable data on backwardness, inadequate representation and administrative efficiency for promotion reservation?
nfc1dc20ae42.x: M. Nagaraj (2006) laid down the quantifiable data requirement; Indra Sawhney ruled out reservation in promotions.

nindian-polity-75-10.s: The concept of 'equality before law' is of ____ origin.
nindian-polity-75-10.x: Equality before law is British and negative in nature; equal protection of the laws is American and positive.

n8983580b942.s: India borrowed the concept of the Rule of Law from:
n8983580b942.x: The Rule of Law, set out by the British jurist A.V. Dicey (1885), came from Britain, like the Cabinet System and Parliamentary Government.

na7e7f1815fa.s: Under Article 16(3), residence requirements for certain public employment may be prescribed by:
na7e7f1815fa.x: Article 16(3) permits Parliament to prescribe residence requirements; Article 16(2) lists descent and residence among prohibited grounds.

nindian-society-45-9.s: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992) upheld a reservation quota for OBCs of:
nindian-society-45-9.x: Indra Sawhney upheld the 27% OBC quota, excluded the creamy layer and set a 50% ceiling.

nindian-society-45-4.s: M. Nagaraj required data on overall administrative efficiency for promotion reservation under Article:
nindian-society-45-4.x: M. Nagaraj (2006) upheld promotion reservation for SCs and STs subject to data on backwardness, inadequate representation and efficiency under Article 335.

nindian-society-45-12.s: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India upheld the 10% EWS quota introduced by the:
nindian-society-45-12.x: Janhit Abhiyan (2022) upheld the 103rd Amendment's 10% EWS quota, accepting economic criteria alone as a valid basis.

nindian-society-9-30.s: General equality of opportunity in public employment is guaranteed by Article:
nindian-society-9-30.x: Article 16(1) guarantees equality of opportunity in public jobs; 16(4) covers reservation and 15(5) educational advancement.

nindian-polity-75-40.s: Which of the following is consistent with the Rule of Law?
o: The ruler remains above the law.
Executive discretion operates without objective standards.
Laws are valid whether or not they are fair.
nindian-polity-75-40.x: Under the Rule of Law, government is bound by law and laws must be just and fair; a ruler above the law belongs to 'rule by law'.

nindian-polity-75-17.s: Which of the following is NOT one of Dicey's three classic elements of the Rule of Law?
o: Primacy of the rights of the individual
nindian-polity-75-17.x: Dicey's elements are absence of arbitrary power, equality before law and primacy of individual rights; people's duty to government is not one.

nindian-polity-75-25.s: Dicey opposed the idea that executive officials should be subject only to:
o: The ordinary law of the land
nindian-polity-75-25.x: Dicey's second element puts everyone under the ordinary law and ordinary courts, so he opposed special tribunals for officials.

nc55110267cc.s: In Balaji Raghavan v. Union of India (1996), the Supreme Court held that Bharat Ratna and Padma awards:
o: May be used as hereditary titles
Are not titles under Article 18, but must not be used as prefixes or suffixes
nc55110267cc.x: The Court held these awards are not titles under Article 18, but they cannot be used as prefixes or suffixes to a name.
